mainTopic: Closing the טומטום discussion, why a father may give a daughter more than a son, and explaining ברייתות about twin births
overview: This amud first finishes the discussion of a טומטום (a child whose gender is unknown). The ברייתא's words 'sustained like a daughter' and 'inherits like a son' are shown to mean only 'fitting to receive, but gets nothing.' Then the גמרא turns to the משנה where a man promises 100 for a son and 200 for a daughter. It asks how a daughter can be preferred, since רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says God is angry at a man who leaves no son. Three answers are given. First, a son is better for inheritance, but a daughter needs more support. Second, שמואל says it is a first birth, and a daughter first is a good sign for sons. Third, the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who says daughters must be fed even more than sons so they won't be shamed. Finally, the גמרא explains two ברייתות about the birth of a boy and a girl. רב אשי explains the first as a reversed gift with an unknown birth order. רבינא begins explaining the second as a reward to whoever brings the news, and he continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can אביי explain 'sustained like a daughter'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if a טומטום does not get a daughter's rights, why does the ברייתא say it is 'sustained like a daughter'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to אביי, what does 'sustained like a daughter' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's opinion about the טומטום using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that a טומטום does not actually receive support the way a daughter does. But the ברייתא clearly says a טומטום is 'sustained like a daughter.' That wording seems to go against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A person whose gender cannot be known

phrases.english: But according to אביי,
what does 'sustained like a daughter' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier אביי / רבא debate about the טומטום from before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that a טומטום does not get a daughter's support
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'sustained like a daughter', which sounds like the טומטום really does get support.

steps.title: Same problem for רבא, so read it as 'fitting but gets nothing'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא has the same problem with 'inherits like a son,' so both phrases must mean 'fitting to receive, but actually gets nothing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, according to רבא, what does 'inherits like a son' mean? Rather, it means he is fitting to inherit, but has nothing. Here too, he is fitting to be sustained, but has nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by showing that רבא would have to read the ברייתא in a softer way too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבא agrees that in this case the טומטום (and the sons) do not actually inherit anything, yet the ברייתא says 'inherits like a son.' So the ברייתא must mean 'has the right in principle, but receives nothing here.' אביי can read 'sustained like a daughter' the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning (turning the question back)
But he does not actually have (anything)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's wording 'like a daughter' and 'like a son' means the טומטום is entitled in principle, even when in practice it gets nothing. So the wording does not disprove אביי.

phrases.english: And by your logic, according to רבא,
what does 'inherits like a son' mean?
Rather, it means he is fitting to inherit, but has nothing;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, רָאוּי לִזּוֹן – וְאֵין לוֹ.
phrases.english: here too, he is fitting to be sustained, but has nothing.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of wording, shown to be needed by both sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sustained like a daughter' means the טומטום actually receives support.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means the טומטום is entitled in principle, as 'inherits like a son' must mean for רבא too.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about a son or daughter being born
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a man who promises one amount if his wife has a boy and another amount if she has a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One who says, 'If my wife gives birth to a male...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the man promises 100 for a son and 200 for a daughter, and each child gets what was promised. The bigger gift for a daughter is what the גמרא is about to ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.english: One who says: If my wife gives birth to
a male, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: a male gets 100 dinars, and a female gets 200 dinars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the טומטום discussion to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever amount was promised for the child who is actually born, that child receives it.

steps.title: Is a daughter really better than a son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a father could prefer a daughter, since רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that God is angry at a man who leaves no son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that he prefers a daughter to a son? But רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: Anyone who does not leave a son to inherit him, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is filled with anger at him. As it says: 'You shall pass his inheritance on to his daughter,' and 'passing on' (העברה) means nothing but anger (עברה), as it says: 'That day is a day of anger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: giving a daughter more seems to show that a daughter is preferred, which goes against a known teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי links the word העברה ('passing on' the inheritance to a daughter) to עברה ('anger'). So leaving only daughters is a sign of God's anger. How could a man treat a daughter as better than a son?

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a doubtful conclusion)
And you shall pass on (the inheritance)

phrases.english: Does this mean that he prefers a daughter to a son?
But רבי יוחנן said
in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי:
Anyone who does not leave a son to inherit him,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא עָלָיו עֶבְרָה,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, is filled with anger at him,
as it says: 'You shall pass his inheritance on to his daughter';
and 'passing on' means nothing but anger,
as it says: 'That day is a day of anger'!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּבַת עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ מִבֵּן? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the משנה quoted in step 3 implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case, where the daughter gets twice as much as the son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A larger gift suggests the daughter is preferred, but רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that having no son is a sign of God's anger.

steps.title: Son for inheritance, daughter for comfort
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: for inheritance a son is better, but for financial comfort and support, a daughter is preferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: For inheritance, a son is better to him. For comfort and support, his daughter is better to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the question into two different areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי was talking about inheritance, and there a son is better. The משנה is about giving extra money for comfort, and there the father prefers to give more to a daughter. So the two sources are not in conflict.
steps.whatToRemember: A son is better for inheritance; a daughter gets more for her comfort. This explains the משנה's bigger gift for a daughter.

phrases.english: For inheritance, a son is better to him.
For comfort and support, his daughter is better to him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two different areas (inheritance vs. support)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bigger gift means the father prefers a daughter over a son in every way.
steps.terutzMaskana: A son is preferred for inheritance; a daughter is given more only for her comfort.

steps.title: שמואל: the משנה is about a first birth
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different answer: the משנה is about a woman giving birth for the first time, and a daughter first is a good sign for sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Here we are dealing with a woman giving birth for the first time, and it follows רב חסדא, who said: A daughter first is a good sign for sons.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל offers a second, separate answer to the question of step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the father does not really prefer daughters. On a first birth he is happier with a girl, because a girl first is a good sign that sons will follow. So the bigger gift actually fits wanting sons.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman giving birth for the first time

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
Here we are dealing with a woman giving birth for the first time,
and it follows רב חסדא,
as רב חסדא said:
A daughter first is a good sign for sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than step 5 to the same challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father simply prefers a daughter over a son.
steps.terutzMaskana: On a first birth a daughter is a good sign that sons will come, so the father is not choosing daughters over sons.

steps.title: Two reasons why a daughter first is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: Two explanations are given: she helps raise her brothers, or the evil eye has no power over the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: because she helps raise her brothers. And some say: because the evil eye has no power over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a first daughter is a good sign for sons, giving two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion is practical: an older sister helps bring up the younger boys. The other is spiritual: a man whose first child is a girl does not attract the evil eye.

phrases.english: Some say: because she helps raise her brothers,
and some say:
because the evil eye has no power over him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the father whose first child is a daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב חסדא's statement in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A first daughter is a good sign either because she helps raise her brothers or because the evil eye has no power over the father.

steps.title: רב חסדא: I personally prefer daughters
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds his personal feeling: he prefers daughters to sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: And as for me, daughters are dearer to me than sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא closes the section with a personal comment about his own family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a legal ruling but a personal preference. It shows that the feelings behind the משנה's case, of a father loving and giving more to a daughter, are real and natural.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are two answers to why the משנה gives more to a daughter: (1) a son is better for inheritance, a daughter for comfort; (2) שמואל: it is a first birth, and a daughter first is a good sign for sons. רב חסדא himself preferred daughters. Step 9 adds a third answer.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
And as for me, daughters are dearer to me than sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A personal remark from רב חסדא, whose teaching was quoted in steps 6 and 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חסדא personally preferred daughters to sons.

steps.title: Another answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a third answer to the question of step 4: our משנה, which prefers a daughter, follows the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer to the question of how the משנה could prefer a daughter. It says the משנה follows the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier answers explained the משנה within everyone's view: daughters are better for support, or a first-born daughter is a good sign. This answer is different. It says the משנה follows one specific תנא, רבי יהודה, who thinks highly of daughters, so it does not have to agree with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another possible answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the קשיא of step 4, alongside the answers in steps 5 and 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to go against רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, who teaches that sons are a must.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who gives daughters a special place.

steps.title: Which teaching of רבי יהודה? Maybe the daughter named 'בכל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי יהודה is meant, and suggests his teaching that אברהם was blessed with a daughter named 'בכל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which teaching of רבי יהודה? If you say it is his teaching about 'בכל', as a ברייתא teaches: 'And ה׳ blessed אברהם with everything (בכל).' רבי מאיר says: the blessing was that he had no daughter. רבי יהודה says: the blessing was that he had a daughter, and her name was 'בכל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which statement of רבי יהודה shows that he prefers daughters. It suggests a first possibility: his teaching that אברהם's blessing was having a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about the פסוק that says אברהם was blessed 'בכל'. רבי מאיר says the blessing was not having a daughter, while רבי יהודה says the blessing was having a daughter named 'בכל'. So רבי יהודה sees a daughter as a blessing, which might be the source for our משנה. This step only sets up the proposal; the next step will test it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a suggestion that is often rejected)
With everything; according to רבי יהודה, also the name of אברהם's daughter

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: He means: which teaching of רבי יהודה shows that he prefers daughters?

phrases.english: If we say the Rabbi Yehuda of "with everything" —
as it is taught: "And the Lord blessed Abraham with everything" —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ בַּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: that he did not have a daughter.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ בַּת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: that he had a daughter,
and her name was "Bakol."

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּ״בַכֹּל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind step 9's claim and suggests a first candidate.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי יהודה shows that he prefers daughters?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First suggestion: his teaching that אברהם was blessed with a daughter named 'בכל'.

steps.title: Rejected: a daughter as a blessing is not better than a son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the 'בכל' source: it only shows that a daughter is a blessing, not that she is better than a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard רבי יהודה say that ה׳ did not hold back even a daughter from אברהם. But did you hear him say that a daughter is better than a son?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 10. The 'בכל' teaching does not prove what our משנה needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, אברהם already had sons, and the blessing was that he got a daughter too. That shows a daughter is something good, but our משנה gives the daughter more than the son. So the 'בכל' teaching is too weak to explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine, say you heard him (say this much)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying רבי יהודה sees no value in a daughter. He clearly sees her as a blessing. The point is only that this does not make her better than a son.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda say

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַתָּא נָמֵי לָא חַסְּרֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא לְאַבְרָהָם;
phrases.english: that the Merciful One did not hold back even a daughter from Abraham;
that she is better than a son, did you hear him say?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source proposed in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'בכל' teaching as the source for step 9's claim, not the claim itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching shows a daughter is a blessing, not that she is preferred over a son.

steps.title: The real source: feeding daughters even more than sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the true source: in a ברייתא, רבי יהודה says that if it is a מצוה to feed sons, it is even more of a מצוה to feed daughters, so they won't be shamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this teaching of רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: it is a מצוה to feed the daughters, and even more so the sons, who learn תורה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: it is a מצוה to feed the sons, and even more so the daughters, so they will not be shamed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better source for step 9. In a מחלוקת about feeding children, רבי יהודה puts the daughters first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says sons come first, because they learn תורה. רבי יהודה turns it around: daughters come first, because without support they could be shamed by having to go begging. Since רבי יהודה ranks daughters above sons here, our משנה, which gives the daughter more, can follow his view.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a logical 'if this, then surely that')
So that they will not be shamed

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה, which favors the daughter, can follow רבי יהודה, because he says daughters must be supported even more than sons so they won't be shamed.

phrases.english: Rather, it is this teaching of Rabbi Yehuda —
as it is taught: It is a מצוה to feed the daughters,
and all the more so the sons,
who are busy learning Torah; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִצְוָה לָזוּן אֶת הַבָּנִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It is a מצוה to feed the sons,
and all the more so the daughters,
so that they will not be shamed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – דְּתַנְיָא: מִצְוָה לָזוּן אֶת הַבָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 11 with a better one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי יהודה shows that he prefers daughters?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His view that daughters must be fed even more than sons, so they won't be shamed.

steps.title: A ברייתא where the son gets more: what case is it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: a ברייתא says that if a boy and a girl were born, the boy gets six dinars and the girl two. What case is that talking about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what a ברייתא teaches: if she gave birth to a boy and a girl, the boy takes six dinars and the girl takes two dinars. What case is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new point and brings a ברייתא that seems to go against our משנה. It asks what case the ברייתא is talking about, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, a man promised 100 if a boy is born and 200 if a girl is born, and when both are born the girl gets more. In this ברייתא, when a boy and a girl are born, the boy gets more. The גמרא wants to know what situation the ברייתא is describing that would explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case? / What are we dealing with?

phrases.english: But what about that which is taught:
If she gave birth to a boy and a girl,
the boy takes six dinars,
phrases.notes: These are gold dinars: six gold ones equal 150 silver, and two equal 50. That's where step 14's numbers come from.

phrases.english: and the girl takes two dinars;
In what case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא: יָלְדָה זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of which תנא the משנה follows and raises a new ברייתא that seems to clash with the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What situation does the ברייתא describe, where the boy gets six dinars and the girl two?

steps.title: רב אשי explains the case as a reversed gift with a doubtful birth order
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי, reporting what he said before רב כהנא, says the ברייתא is about one who reversed his conditions: a boy first gets 200 and a girl after him gets nothing, but a girl first gets 100 and a boy after her gets 100. Twins were born and the order is unknown. The boy takes 100 for sure, and the other 100 is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב כהנא: it is about a man who reversed his conditions. He said: 'If a boy is born first, he gets 200 and a girl after him gets nothing. If a girl is born first, she gets 100 and a boy after her gets 100.' The mother had a boy and a girl, and we don't know who came out first. The boy takes 100 no matter what. The other 100 is money in doubt, so they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 13 by describing the exact case behind the ברייתא about a boy and a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both possible birth orders the boy gets at least 100, so that much is his for sure. Only the second 100 is in question, since it goes to the boy if he came first and to the girl if she came first. Because we can't know, they split it. The boy ends up with 150 and the girl with 50, which matches the ברייתא's six gold dinars (150 silver) and two gold dinars (50 silver).

keyTerms.meaning: One who reverses or mixes up his conditions, so that being born first doesn't always help
Whichever way you look at it; either way

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of doubtful money: whatever a person gets in every possible case is his for sure, and only the uncertain part is divided.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said this teaching before Rav Kahana:
It is about one who reversed his conditions,
who said: 'If a male is born first – two hundred,'
'a female after him – nothing at all.'
'A female first – one hundred,'
'a male after her – one hundred.'
And she gave birth to a male and a female,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִינַן הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ נְפַק בְּרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: and we don't know which of them came out first.
The male takes one hundred either way,
phrases.notes: If he came first he gets 200, and if he came second he gets 100, so 100 is his no matter what.

phrases.aramaic: אִידַּךְ מָנֶה – הָוֵה מָמוֹן הַמּוּטָּל בְּסָפֵק,
phrases.english: the other hundred is money whose owner is in doubt,
and they split it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by giving the exact case of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is the ברייתא about, where a boy and a girl were born and each gets a set amount?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A reversed gift (מסרס) with an unknown birth order: the boy takes 100 for sure and the doubtful 100 is split.

steps.title: Asking about another ברייתא where 'he' gets only one hundred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא: if she gave birth to a boy and a girl, 'he' gets only a מנה, even though two children were born. It asks what case that could be.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about the other ברייתא that says: if she gave birth to a boy and a girl, he gets only 100? How can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a second ברייתא and asks what kind of case it is describing. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says that when a boy and a girl are born, 'he' gets only one מנה. It does not say who 'he' is or why. The גמרא asks what kind of promise would lead to that result, and the next step answers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first ברייתא, now explained, to a second ברייתא that needs its own case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case would give 'him' only 100 when a boy and a girl are born?

steps.title: רבינא begins: a case of 'whoever brings me the news'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the second ברייתא is about a man who promised money to whoever brings him the news of the birth (מבשרני). The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is about a man who said 'whoever brings me the news.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts to answer step 15 by naming the kind of promise behind the ברייתא. The full explanation comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא moves the ברייתא away from a gift to the children. It is about a reward promised to whoever brings the father the news of the birth. So the 'he' who gets only 100 is the one who brings the news, and the details follow on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: '(Whoever) brings me the news'; a promise to reward the one who announces the birth

phrases.english: Ravina said: It is about 'whoever informs me' –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A case of מבשרני, where the father promised a reward to whoever brings him the news (explained further in what follows).
